scope: Each row received at least one current primary homepage, pricing, support or README read. These are publisher-stated plans/features, not runtime/security/checkout measurements. Major live pricing modes and unresolved contradictions are labeled. Previous reports and benchmark files remain unchanged.

vendors.name: Screenpipe
vendors.plans: Free: limited recent history. Basic: $250/year (page rounds to $21/month). Business: $500/seat/year (about $42/month). Enterprise: custom. Max/Ultra capacity prices not verified.
vendors.features: Screen, microphone/system audio, OCR and Accessibility text; timeline, search, AI questions, MCP, scheduled workflows, meeting reminders, saved model presets and narrated SOP exports.
vendors.models: Local/Ollama and supported cloud providers or own API credentials. Capture, cloud transcription, model requests, sync and connected apps have separate data paths. Local and enclave privacy-filter options.
vendors.difference: Broad capture-to-automation reference. Personal cross-device sync is Business; shared teammate context and managed controls require Enterprise. Current source uses a commercial license, including restrictions on competing products.
vendors.caveat: Publisher estimates for storage and RAM conflict across pages. Enclave processing sends selected text off-device. No current desktop binary, power or checkout validation.

vendors.name: Original Rewind / Limitless
vendors.plans: No new Pendant sales. Existing Pendant customers receive Unlimited without subscription fees through 2026. Historical meeting access continues through 2026.
vendors.features: Original desktop visual/audio memory is a historical design reference. Rewind screen and audio capture was disabled on December 19, 2025; Limitless desktop/web can no longer record.
vendors.models: The continuing offering is for existing Pendant customers. Export and account-deletion paths are documented.
vendors.difference: A migration and preservation target for OSwind, rather than an available new desktop-memory subscription.
vendors.caveat: Some regions lost service in December 2025. Do not confuse this product with the separate rewind.app site.

vendors.name: Rewind Desktop / rewind.app
vendors.plans: Current homepage does not publish a price. Older article pricing is not treated as a current quote.
vendors.features: Continuous screen recording, local text search, visual result selection and timeline scrubbing. Optional personal Amazon S3 archive.
vendors.models: Publisher says video and recovery backups are encrypted locally before upload; older video downloads on demand while text remains searchable locally.
vendors.difference: Emphasizes visual recall with storage ownership and optional archival offload.
vendors.caveat: No account, encrypted-archive recovery, current paid tier or runtime test. Distinct from original Rewind/Limitless.

vendors.name: Pieces
vendors.plans: Pro: $18.99/user/month. Enterprise: $22.99/user/month or $69.99/user/quarter as displayed. Seven-day trial requires a card; no free plan. Annual selection not verified.
vendors.features: On-device long-term work memory; app/site capture; chronological recall scoped by time, topic, person or tool; recaps, meeting prep, morning briefs and unlimited MCP.
vendors.models: Per-question hosted-model selection and local models are advertised. Enterprise adds approved providers, own API keys and organization capture/feature policy.
vendors.difference: Memory distributed into existing assistants through MCP, with a large ready-made summary catalog.
vendors.caveat: On-device memory does not establish that model inference is always local. Current claims and monthly pricing were reviewed, without a runtime or checkout audit.

vendors.name: Littlebird
vendors.plans: Basic: free. Plus: $204/year. Power: $510/year. Pro selected 5× tier: $100/month; other tier not priced here. Team: from $17/seat/month annual. Enterprise: custom.
vendors.features: Basic has 25 total meeting notes, five routines and two Max messages/day. Plus has unlimited meeting notes, 100 routines, MCP and monthly credits. Power doubles Plus credits; Pro adds Ultra mode.
vendors.models: Foreground-app context, chosen bot-free meetings and optional connected apps. Memory is stored in AWS US East; relevant context is sent to AI providers.
vendors.difference: Strong routines, meeting preparation, contextual assistance and connected-work tooling. Enterprise adds SSO.
vendors.caveat: Cloud memory is explicit; this is not a local-only architecture. Credits and model modes are not comparable to fixed token or request allowances.

vendors.name: Microsoft Recall
vendors.plans: No separate Recall subscription is documented on the reviewed support page. Requires supported Windows 11 Copilot+ hardware.
vendors.features: Opt-in snapshots, visual/text semantic search, explorable timeline, source reopening, app/site filtering, pause and deletion.
vendors.models: Local encrypted snapshot storage protected by Windows Hello. Requirements include a 40-TOPS NPU, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB storage, device encryption and biometric enhanced sign-in.
vendors.difference: OS-integrated visual retrieval and authentication. At least 50 GB free is needed to enable; saving pauses below 25 GB.
vendors.caveat: Windows reference rather than a Mac competitor. No matched hardware, retrieval-quality or energy test; no BYOK path established by this page.

vendors.name: ScreenMemory
vendors.plans: Free card lists both 24-hour and unlimited history, a contradiction. Standard: $29, one year of updates, three devices, optional $5/year renewal. Lifetime: $39 once.
vendors.features: Screenshot history, scrubbable timeline, app filtering, on-device OCR search, calendar heatmaps, app blacklist and paid multi-monitor capture.
vendors.models: Local storage and OCR. Periodic network license verification is described.
vendors.difference: Simple visual history and low one-time pricing. Three licensed devices do not imply synchronized history.
vendors.caveat: Publisher says encryption at rest is planned. Its 280 MB/day example assumes eight hours and 60-second captures; it is not a matched OSwind measurement.

vendors.name: TimeScroll
vendors.plans: Free download and source project.
vendors.features: Color-coded app timeline, keyword search with highlighted locations, app/date filters, semantic image search, optional microphone/system-audio transcripts, MCP and app exclusions.
vendors.models: MobileCLIP2 on-device or local Ollama embeddings; local Whisper. Accessibility text mode avoids OCR, near-duplicates are skipped and capture backs off when hot.
vendors.difference: Native Swift, Mac 14+, Intel and Apple Silicon; database/media encrypted-vault feature is labeled beta.
vendors.caveat: Energy savings and capture quality are publisher claims here. No matched power, vault-security or current runtime audit.

vendors.name: Retrace / haseab
vendors.plans: Public MIT source; no paid plan documented in the reviewed README.
vendors.features: Configurable captures, Apple Vision OCR, FTS5, timeline, app/date/exclusion filters, dashboard, Rewind import, hotkeys, HEVC storage and result highlighting.
vendors.models: Local Apple Silicon Mac app. README marks audio as disabled, semantic embeddings as prepared but inactive, and stored-data encryption as in progress.
vendors.difference: Clear visual-history and migration reference, with an explicit early-development status.
vendors.caveat: README reports 50–70 GB/month and targets 15–20 GB/month; these are publisher figures and a target, not measured current parity or energy results.

vendors.name: Retrace / jhammant
vendors.plans: Public source; README advertises Apache-2.0. No paid plan established.
vendors.features: Timeline, text/semantic/hybrid search, app/domain activity stats, CPU/RAM charts, read-only MCP, exclusions, hidden/pause mode and bounded retention.
vendors.models: On-device OS frameworks: Accessibility/OCR, captions and embeddings. Raw frames are transient; thumbnails and derived context remain. Lock, idle and display sleep pause capture.
vendors.difference: A Mac/Windows reference for a lightweight derived timeline, rather than full-resolution raw-frame retention.
vendors.caveat: README claims and platform paths were reviewed; local-only behavior, image deletion and resource claims were not independently exercised.

vendors.name: rem
vendors.plans: Public source/download; no paid tier established by the reviewed README.
vendors.features: Two-second screenshots, text recognition, video timeline scrubbing, historical text copying, keyword/app search and copying recent context into an LLM prompt.
vendors.models: Local history. README lists semantic search and agent interaction as future work; Intel builds are available, with the author primarily testing Apple Silicon.
vendors.difference: Small native visual-memory reference and a useful lexical baseline.
vendors.caveat: The README labels it very early alpha. Copying context into another AI is distinct from integrated local RAG. Current app behavior was not retested.

vendors.name: Unlost
vendors.plans: Public source/download; no current paid plan established in the reviewed README.
vendors.features: Semantic recall and questions over seen content, meeting-transcript search, screenshot crop-to-copy and reopening captured websites. Zoom and Google Meet transcripts are listed.
vendors.models: SwiftUI capture/OCR with a local Python indexing and semantic-search server using txtai.
vendors.difference: An earlier combined screenshot and meeting-memory design.
vendors.caveat: The reviewed README was last modified in 2024. Remote-server offload is described as future work; no modern runtime or energy acceptance follows.

vendors.name: Pensieve / formerly Memos
vendors.plans: Public source; self-hosted model, provider and infrastructure costs remain separate.
vendors.features: Screen capture, full-text/vector retrieval, app blacklist, URL metadata, chronological entity detail, configuration UI, plugins and an agent search skill.
vendors.models: Ollama and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, including Azure/vLLM. SQLite and optional PostgreSQL/pgvector support; Mac and Windows are listed, Linux remains in development.
vendors.difference: Flexible retrieval/storage backend and extensibility, with more setup work than a packaged native Mac app.
vendors.caveat: Local storage does not make a selected cloud model local. No fresh runtime, large-database or power benchmark was performed for this refresh.

vendors.name: Minne
vendors.plans: Free, MIT-licensed Mac app. External provider billing or local-model resources are separate.
vendors.features: Accessibility text memory distilled into editable Markdown notes for people, projects and days; contextual reply drafts, memory chat and explicit insertion/undo.
vendors.models: Own Claude/ChatGPT sign-in or local Ollama. Publisher describes masked capture batches being sent to the chosen model for note distillation, plus task-specific draft/chat context.
vendors.difference: Portable plain files and a focused writing loop. No screenshot/video history.
vendors.caveat: Local note storage is separate from provider processing. Publisher's masking and no-telemetry claims were reviewed without a runtime security audit.

vendors.name: Omi
vendors.plans: Direct wearable offer: $169 device. Free: unlimited phone recording, five cloud hours/month and 30 questions/month. Pro: $29.99/month or $269.91/year, advertised 1,000 questions/month.
vendors.features: Conversation transcription, summaries, tasks, speaker features, live text, offline wearable recording, calendar/email/task integrations, MCP and real-time meeting assistance on desktop.
vendors.models: Open-source project and local-run options are advertised; the direct offer includes cloud allowances and provider integrations.
vendors.difference: Wearable/mobile/desktop conversation ecosystem. Mac download does not require buying a device.
vendors.caveat: These prices and allowances come from the wearable offer; desktop-only entitlement is not verified. A redirected offer URL failed; the main offer and support pages were readable.

vendors.name: Granola
vendors.plans: Basic: $0, 30-day meeting history. Business: $14/user/month. Enterprise: $35/user/month as displayed.
vendors.features: Bot-free meeting notes, speaker tagging, templates, voice typing, multilingual support and cross-meeting chat. Paid tiers add unlimited history, model choice, briefs, integrations, expanded MCP and API access.
vendors.models: Audio is deleted after transcription according to the plan table. User model-training opt-out is available; Enterprise defaults and organization policy differ.
vendors.difference: Meeting productivity and collaboration reference, not a full desktop visual-history recorder.
vendors.caveat: Free MCP is limited to personal notes from the last 30 days. No transcript, consent-flow, security or billing checkout test was performed.

vendors.name: OpenRecall
vendors.plans: Public AGPLv3 source; no subscription documented in the reviewed README.
vendors.features: Periodic snapshots, local OCR/semantic search, timeline browsing, configurable storage path and multi-monitor capture with a primary-monitor-only option.
vendors.models: Local Python application with browser UI, targeting Windows, macOS and Linux. Documentation recommends a separately encrypted volume for storage protection.
vendors.difference: Cross-platform local visual memory with a straightforward self-hosted shape.
vendors.caveat: External-volume encryption guidance is distinct from an app-managed vault. No current release, model-quality or energy audit.

vendors.name: OpenHistory
vendors.plans: Public source and Mac download; no paid plan stated on the reviewed homepage.
vendors.features: Foreground-app and permitted Accessibility context, daily timelines, summaries, grounded agent retrieval, app/category exclusions and independent email/messaging controls.
vendors.models: No screenshots, microphone, camera or keystroke recording. Optional Apple on-device summaries need compatible hardware and macOS 26; OpenAI/Anthropic/Kimi use explicit BYOK.
vendors.difference: Authenticated local MCP exposes redacted read-only timelines rather than the raw activity log. Mac app itself supports macOS 14+.
vendors.caveat: Publisher claims were refreshed; redaction, deletion, provider isolation and runtime behavior were not independently tested.

vendors.name: silverfish
vendors.plans: Public source; local Ollama runtime, model storage and hardware are separate costs.
vendors.features: Accessibility text capture, FTS5, hierarchical recaps, people/project/tool graph, distilled wiki and identity profile, chat, briefs, inline rewrites and MCP.
vendors.models: Four configurable Ollama roles: fast, chat, summarize and heavy. Hardware-aware onboarding recommends models; README says inference endpoints must be loopback.
vendors.difference: All-local text-memory and model-routing reference. No screenshots. Rust daemon, CLI and menu-bar app.
vendors.caveat: The default model set is publisher-estimated at roughly 33 GB. No fresh process/network isolation, model-sizing or energy measurement.

vendors.name: Goldfish
vendors.plans: Free during beta. No post-beta price published on the reviewed homepage.
vendors.features: Accessibility text memory, personalized writing drafts, memory chat, context for existing assistants, dictation and background memory organization; Mac and Windows.
vendors.models: Local database, with selected text sent for foreground and background AI through Cloudflare to a private Azure OpenAI deployment, according to its privacy policy.
vendors.difference: Low-friction writing assistance and automatic integration with common AI clients.
vendors.caveat: Local history does not mean local inference. Publisher says masking is imperfect and omits some ordinary personal details; product analytics opt-out requires contacting support.
